title: Essential VS Code extensions
content:
Introduction: VS Code, the universal editor

VS Code dominates the code editor market with 70%+ of developers using it daily. Why this craze?
  • Lightweight and fast (unlike IntelliJ/Eclipse)
  • Extensions for EVERYTHING (languages, frameworks, tools)
  • Open source (Microsoft)
  • Infinitely customizable
  • Integrated with Git, Docker, SSH...
But poorly configured, VS Code remains basic. Well equipped, it becomes a powerful IDE.

1️⃣ Code quality (required)

Prettier (auto format)

  • Automatic formatting: indentation, quotes, semicolons...
  • Supports JS, TS, CSS, HTML, JSON, Markdown...
  • Config via .prettierrc
Recommended settings (settings.json): ```json { "editor.formatOnSave": true, "editor.defaultFormatter": "esbenp.prettier-vscode" } ```

ESLint (JS/TS linting)

  • Detects potential errors
  • Forces consistent code style
  • Auto-fix possible (Cmd+Shift+P → ESLint: Fix all)
Enable auto-fix: ```json { "editor.codeActionsOnSave": { "source.fixAll.eslint": true } } ```

Error Lens (inline errors)

Shows TypeScript/ESLint errors directly in the line (no need for hover).

2️⃣ Git & Versioning

GitLens (Superloaded Git)

  • See who modified which line (blame inline)
  • File history (timeline)
  • Compare commits
  • Branch graph

Git Graph (view branches)

Alternative to GitLens for a visual graph of commits and branches.

3️⃣ Web Development

Live Server (auto reload)

Starts a local server with hot reload instantaneously. Right click on index.html → “Open with Live Server”.

Auto Rename Tag

Automatically renames related HTML/JSX tags. Example: Change <div> to <section> → close automatically updated.

REST Client (testing APIs)

Creates a file .http: ```http GET https://api.github.com/users/github Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN ``` Click on “Send Request” → response in VS Code (goodbye Postman).

Tailwind CSS IntelliSense

Auto-completion of Tailwind classes + color preview.

4️⃣ Productivity & Navigation

Path Intellisense

Auto-completion of file paths (imports, images...).

TODO Highlight

Highlights TODO, FIXME, HACK in the code.

Better Comments

Comments colored by type: ```js // ! Danger // ? Question // TODO: À faire // * Important ```

5️⃣ Appearance & Themes

Material Icon Theme

Material Design icons for files (very readable).

Popular themes

  • Dracula Official: Dark, purple
  • One Dark Pro: Inspired by Atom
  • Night Owl: Optimized for night
  • GitHub Theme: Light/dark like GitHub

6️⃣ Specific languages

Python

  • Python (Microsoft): IntelliSense, linting, debugging
  • Pylance: Quick type checking

Docker

  • Docker: Syntax highlighting Dockerfile, manage containers

Markdown

  • Markdown All in One: Shortcuts, preview, auto TOC
  • Markdown Preview Enhanced: GitHub style preview, PDF/HTML export, diagrams

JSON

  • JSON Crack: Visualize JSON in graphical format (DB-type relational diagram)

7️⃣ AI & Code Support

GitHub Copilot

  • AI auto-completion (contextual suggestions)
  • Generation complete functions
  • 10$/month (free students/open-source)

Codeium

  • Free alternative to Copilot
  • Multi-language support
  • Integrated AI chat

Continue (Ollama local)

  • Local LLM (Llama, Mistral, CodeLlama)
  • 100% private (no cloud)
  • Free, open-source
  • Requires Ollama installed

8️⃣ Docker & Containers

Docker (official extension)

  • Syntax highlighting Dockerfile
  • Manage containers/images from VS Code
  • Container logs in real time

Dev Containers

  • Develop IN a Docker container
  • Isolated and reproducible environment
  • Config via .devcontainer/devcontainer.json

🎯 Conclusion

A good VS Code setup = massive productivity gain. Must-haves by category:
  • Quality: Prettier, ESLint, Error Lens
  • Git: GitLens
  • Web: Live Server, Tailwind IntelliSense, REST Client
  • Productivity: Path Intellisense, TODO Highlight
  • Markdown: Markdown Preview Enhanced
  • JSON: JSON Crack
  • AI: Copilot or Codeium (Continuous for local)
  • Docker: Docker + Dev Containers
> “Productivity does not come from more work, but from better tools.” 🚀

title: Organize your tech monitoring effectively
content:
Introduction: Staying up to date without going under

Tech evolves ultra-fast: new JS framework every week, major updates, vulnerabilities... Problem: Without organization, monitoring becomes a source of stress (dozens of open tabs never read). Solution: A structured and regular monitoring system.

1️⃣ Centralize sources

RSS aggregators

  • Feedly: Brings together blogs, official docs, YouTube
  • Inoreader: More advanced (filters, rules)
  • NewsBlur: Open source, self-hosted
Example of RSS feed to follow:
  • dev.to/feed
  • css-tricks.com/feed
  • blog.cloudflare.com/rss
  • github.blog/feed

Tech Newsletters

  • TLDR: Daily summary (tech, dev, crypto, AI)
  • JavaScript Weekly: JS News
  • DevOps Weekly: DevOps Tools and Practices
  • Hacker Newsletter: Top posts from Hacker News

Social networks

  • Twitter/X: Creates lists (eg: "Frontend devs")
  • Reddit: r/programming, r/webdev, r/devops
  • LinkedIn: Follow experts (Kent C. Dodds, Dan Abramov...)
  • YouTube: Fireship, Theo, Traversy Media

2️⃣ Structure by categories

Creates clear categories

  • Frontend: React, Vue, CSS, UI/UX
  • Backend: Node.js, APIs, databases
  • DevOps: Docker, CI/CD, Kubernetes
  • Tools: VS Code, Git, CLI tools
  • Security: Vulnerabilities, best practices
  • AI/ML: ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, trends

Backup tools

  • Notion: Database of links with tags
  • Raindrop.io: Organized bookmarks
  • Pocket: Simple read-it-later
  • Obsidian: Connected notes (second brain)

3️⃣ Plan your sleep (time-boxing)

Fixed weekly slot

Example: Friday morning, 9 a.m.-9:30 a.m.
  • Browse Feedly (10 min)
  • Read 2-3 tagged articles (15 min)
  • Save to Notion (5 min)

Passive sleep

  • In-Car/Transportation Podcasts (Syntax.fm, Changelog)
  • YouTube videos during lunch break (Fireship, ThePrimeagen)

4️⃣ Filter the essentials

Rule of 3 filters

  • Is this actionable? (Can I apply it now?)
  • Is this relevant? (Related to my projects/stack?)
  • Is this verified? (Trusted source?)
If NO to all 3 → skip.

Avoid FOMO

You CAN NOT track everything. Rather than reading everything, focus on your main stack + 1-2 emerging technologies.

5️⃣ Learn by doing

Learn in public

  • Write a Twitter thread/X: Explain what you learned
  • Publish a blog post: Summary + examples
  • Create a mini-project: Test the new tool/framework
Principle: What we explain, we remember 3x better.

Collaborative monitoring

  • Create a Slack/Discord channel with your team
  • Everyone shares 1-2 links per week
  • Weekly review: "This week I learned..."

6️⃣ Complete Workflow Example

Monday morning (5 min)

  • Read TLDR newsletter
  • Mark 2-3 interesting articles

Wednesday break (10 min)

  • Read 1 article tagged
  • Take 3 notes in Notion

Friday afternoon (30 min)

  • Feedly: browse feeds (15 min)
  • Read 1 full technical article (10 min)
  • Test a tool/lib (5 min)

🎯 Conclusion

Good monitoring = regularity + filtering. The 3 golden rules:
  • Centralize (Feedly + newsletters)
  • Schedules (fixed weekly slot)
  • Share (learn in public)
> “30 minutes a week is better than 3 hours of binge-reading on Sunday evening.” 📚

title: Improve your productivity with simple Bash scripts
content:
Introduction: Automate repetitive tasks

Do you type the same commands every day? Examples:
  • rm -rf node_modules && npm install
  • git add . && git commit -m "fix" && git push
  • docker stop $(docker ps -q)
Rather than retyping them, automates it with Bash. Bash = The Unix/Linux scripting language (also available on macOS and Windows via Git Bash/WSL).

1️⃣ Script 1: Clean up a Node.js project

Problem

Node_modules corrupted? Need to reinstall the deps properly?

Script: clean.sh

```bash #!/bin/bash echo "🧹 Nettoyage en cours..." rm -rf node_modules rm -rf package-lock.json echo "📦 Reinstalling dependencies..." npm install echo "✅ Terminé !" ```

Usage

```bash chmod +x clean.sh ./clean.sh ```

2️⃣ Script 2: Quick deployment (Git)

Problem

Typing git add, commit, push each time = time consuming.

Script: deploy.sh

```bash #!/bin/bash if [ -z "$1" ]; then echo "⚠️ Usage: ./deploy.sh \"commit message\"" exit 1 fi echo "🚀 Deploying..." git add . git commit -m "$1" git push origin main echo "✅ Pushed to main!" ```

Usage

```bash ./deploy.sh "fix: corrige le bug de login" ```

3️⃣ Script 3: Autosave

Problem

You want to save your projects regularly.

Script: backup.sh

```bash #!/bin/bash DATE=$(date +%F) BACKUP_DIR=~/backups mkdir -p $BACKUP_DIR echo "💾 Backing up the ~/projects directory..." tar -czvf $BACKUP_DIR/backup_$DATE.tar.gz ~/projects echo "✅ Backup created : $BACKUP_DIR/backup_$DATE.tar.gz" ```

Automation (cron)

Run this script every day at 11 p.m.: ```bash crontab -e # Add this line : 0 23 * * * ~/bin/backup.sh ```

4️⃣ Script 4: Kill all Docker containers

Problem

Lots of rotating containers, you want to stop everything.

Script: docker-clean.sh

```bash #!/bin/bash echo "🐳 Stopping all containers..." docker stop $(docker ps -q) echo "🧹 Removing stopped containers..." docker container prune -f echo "✅ Nettoyage terminé !" ```

5️⃣ Make your scripts accessible everywhere

Step 1: Create a ~/bin folder

```bash mkdir -p ~/bin ```

Step 2: Add ~/bin to PATH

In ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc: ```bash export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH" ``` Recharge: ```bash source ~/.bashrc ```

Step 3: Place your scripts in ~/bin

```bash mv deploy.sh ~/bin/deploy chmod +x ~/bin/deploy ``` Now you can run deploy from anywhere!

6️⃣ Bash Best Practices

  • ✅ Shebang: Always start with #!/bin/bash
  • ✅ Check arguments: if [ -z "$1" ]
  • ✅ Quotes: Use "$VAR" instead of $VAR
  • ✅ Exit codes: exit 1 in case of error
  • ✅ set -e: Stops the script if a command fails

🎯 Conclusion

Some Bash scripts = hours saved. The 3 main use cases:
  • Cleaning/installation (clean.sh)
  • Quick deployment (deploy.sh)
  • Recurring automation (backup.sh + cron)
> “The best code is the one you only write once.” ⚙️

title: Write clear documentation in Markdown (README, Wiki, etc.)
content:
Introduction: The universal language of documentation

Markdown is THE format for writing documentation: README, wikis, blogs, changelogs, GitHub issues... Why Markdown?
  • Readable even in plain text
  • Compatible everywhere (GitHub, GitLab, Notion, Discord...)
  • Releasable with Git
  • Convertible to HTML/PDF
  • Quick to write (no buttons, just text)

1️⃣ Essential Syntax

Titles

```markdown # H1 - Titre principal ## H2 - Section ### H3 - Sous-section ```

Text formatting

```markdown **bold** or __bold__ *italic* or _italic_ ~~barré~~ `code inline` ```

Lists

```markdown - Unordered list - Item 2 - Sous-item 1. Ordered list 2. Item 2 ```

Links and images

```markdown [Link text](https://example.com) ![Alt text](image.png) ```

Code blocks

\`\`\`javascript const hello = () => { console.log("Hello!"); }; \`\`\`

Quotes

```markdown > This is a quote > Across multiple lines ```

Tables

```markdown | Column 1 | Column 2 | |-----------|-----------| | Data 1 | Data 2 | ```

2️⃣ Structure of a good README

Recommended template

```markdown # Project Name Short, clear project description. ## 🚀 Installation \`\`\`bash npm install npm start \`\`\` ## 📖 Utilisation Code examples... ## ✨ Features - Feature 1 - Feature 2 ## 🛠️ Stack technique - React 18 - TypeScript - Tailwind CSS ## 🤝 Contributing Pull requests welcome! ## 📝 License MIT ```

3️⃣ Best practices

  • ✅ Clear title: # My Project
  • ✅ Table of contents for long docs
  • ✅ Screenshots or GIFs to view
  • ✅ Concrete code examples
  • ✅ Badges (build status, version...)
  • ✅ Links to docs detailed if necessary

4️⃣ Tools and extensions

Editors

  • VS Code: Integrated Preview (Cmd+Shift+V)
  • Obsidian: Related notes (second brain)
  • Typora: WYSIWYG Markdown

Doc generators

  • MkDocs: Static site from Markdown
  • Docusaurus: Docs React (Meta)
  • VitePress: Docs Vue/Vite
  • GitBook: Hosted platform

VS Code Extensions

  • Markdown All in One: Shortcuts, auto TOC, preview
  • markdownlint: Linting Markdown

5️⃣ Advanced Markdown (GitHub Flavored)

Task lists

```markdown - [x] Task completed - [ ] Task in progress ```

Alerts/Admonitions

On GitHub: ```markdown > [!NOTE] > Useful information > [!WARNING] > Critical warning ```

Mermaid diagrams

```markdown \`\`\`mermaid graph TD A[Start] --> B[Process] B --> C[End] \`\`\` ```

🎯 Conclusion

Markdown = effective communication without complexity. The 3 golden rules:
  • Simple and clear
  • Concrete examples
  • Logical structure
> “A good doc is worth a thousand meetings.” 📚

title: Use GitHub Projects to manage your side projects
content:
Introduction: GitHub Native Project Management

GitHub Projects = Kanban/Roadmap integrated directly into GitHub. Advantages:
  • No need for separate Trello/Jira/Notion
  • Issues and PRs automatically synchronized
  • Free for public AND private rest
  • Built-in automations

1️⃣ Create a project

Steps:
  • "Projects" tab in your repository
  • "New project" → Choose template (Board, Table, Roadmap)
  • Customize columns
Available templates:
  • Board: Classic Kanban (To Do, In Progress, Done)
  • Table: Spreadsheet view (filters, sorting)
  • Roadmap: Timeline with dates

2️⃣ Add items

Existing Issues

Drag & drop from the issue list.

Draft items

Creates quick notes (converted to issues later).

Pull Requests

PRs appear automatically if linked to an issue.

3️⃣ Custom fields

Adds custom fields:
  • Priority: High, Medium, Low
  • Size: Small, Medium, Large
  • Sprint: Sprint 1, Sprint 2...
  • Assignee: Who is working on it

4️⃣ Automations

Built-in workflows

  • Open issue → Auto-add to "To Do"
  • PR merged → Move to "Done"
  • Issue closed → Archive automatically

GitHub Actions

Automate with workflows: ```yaml name: Add to Project on: issues: types: [opened] jobs: add-to-project: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/add-to-project@v0.5.0 with: project-url: https://github.com/users/USER/projects/1 ```

5️⃣ Labels and filters

Recommended labels

  • feature 🟢: New feature
  • bug 🔴: Bug fix
  • docs 📘: Documentation
  • refactor ♻️: Code cleanup
  • urgent 🚨: High priority

Powerful filters

  • label:bug status:"In Progress"
  • assignee:@me
  • is:open is:pr

6️⃣ Multiple views

Creates multiple views of the same project:
  • Kanban view: For daily workflow
  • Table View: For advanced sorting/filtering
  • Roadmap view: For long-term planning

🎯 Conclusion

GitHub Projects = Simplified Jira, perfect for side projects and small teams. Best practices:
  • An outcome = a clear task
  • Consistent labels
  • Automates everything that can be
> “The best project management is the one you really use.” 📋

title: Create a productive terminal setup (Oh My Zsh, Starship, aliases…)
content:
Introduction: The terminal, your daily HQ

You spend hours a day in the terminal. Might as well make it fast, beautiful and efficient. Objectives:
  • Super-fast browsing
  • Intelligent autocomplete
  • Prompt informative but minimalist
  • Aliases for frequent commands

1️⃣ Choose your shell

Bash vs Zsh

  • Bash: Default on Linux, stable
  • Zsh: More modern, better autocompletion, themes
Recommendation: Zsh (macOS default since Catalina). Install Zsh: ```bash # macOS brew install zsh # Linux sudo apt install zsh # Set as the default shell chsh -s $(which zsh) ```

2️⃣ Oh My Zsh (Zsh framework)

Installation

```bash sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/master/tools/install.sh)" ```

Essential Plugins

In ~/.zshrc: ```bash plugins=( git z zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting docker npm ) ``` Description:
  • git: Aliases (gst, gco, gpl...)
  • z : Jump to frequent dirs (z my-project)
  • autosuggestions: Suggestions based on history
  • syntax-highlighting: Coloring commands
Install external plugins: ```bash git clone https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-~/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions git clone https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting ${ZSH_CUSTOM:-~/.oh-my-zsh/custom}/plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting ```

3️⃣ Starship Prompt

Installation

```bash curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh ``` Adds to ~/.zshrc: ```bash eval "$(starship init zsh)" ```

Why Starship?

  • Super fast (written in Rust)
  • Multi-shell (Bash, Zsh, Fish...)
  • Displays: Git branch, Node version, Python env...
  • Highly customizable

Custom Config

Creates ~/.config/starship.toml: ```toml [character] success_symbol = "[➜](bold green)" error_symbol = "[✗](bold red)" [git_branch] format = "on [$symbol$branch]($style) " style = "bold purple" ```

4️⃣ Powerful aliases

In ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc: ```bash # Git alias gs='git status' alias ga='git add' alias gc='git commit -m' alias gp='git push' alias gl='git log --oneline --graph --decorate' # Navigation alias ..='cd ..' alias ...='cd ../..' alias ll='ls -lah' # Docker alias dps='docker ps' alias dstop='docker stop $(docker ps -q)' alias dclean='docker system prune -af' # Dev alias serve='python3 -m http.server 8080' alias weather='curl wttr.in' ```

5️⃣ Modern CLI Tools

  • bat: cat with syntax highlighting
  • exa: modern ls
  • fzf: Interactive fuzzy finder
  • tldr: Simplified man pages
Install: ```bash brew install bat exa fzf tldr ``` Aliases: ```bash alias cat='bat' alias ls='exa --icons' alias find='fzf' ```

🎯 Conclusion

A well configured terminal = massive speed gain. Minimum recommended setup:
  • Zsh + Oh My Zsh
  • Starship prompt
  • Custom Aliases
  • fzf + bat + exa
> “The terminal is not an obstacle, it is an accelerator.” ⚡

title: Manage your secrets and API keys locally without risk
content:
Introduction: NEVER commit secrets

Putting your API keys in a public repo is a fatal error. Risks:
  • Account compromise (astronomical AWS bills)
  • Unauthorized access to customer data
  • Automatic scanners search for secrets on GitHub

1️⃣ .env files

Create .env

```bash # .env DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_xxxxxxxxxxxxx JWT_SECRET=super-secret-key-change-me API_KEY=abcd1234efgh5678 ```

Add to .gitignore

```bash # .gitignore .env .env.local .env.*.local ```

Create .env.example

Public template for the team: ```bash # .env.example DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/dbname STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_your_key_here JWT_SECRET=change-me API_KEY=your-api-key ```

2️⃣ Use env variables

Node.js

```javascript // Install dotenv npm install dotenv // app.js require('dotenv').config(); const apiKey = process.env.API_KEY; const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL; ```

Python

```python # Install python-dotenv pip install python-dotenv # app.py from dotenv import load_dotenv import os load_dotenv() api_key = os.getenv('API_KEY') db_url = os.getenv('DATABASE_URL') ```

React/Vite

Prefix VITE_ required: ```bash # .env VITE_API_URL=https://api.example.com VITE_GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID=G-XXXXXXXXXX ``` ```javascript // src/config.ts export const API_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL; ```

3️⃣ GitHub Secrets (CI/CD)

For GitHub Actions workflows: Steps:
  • Repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
  • New repository secret
  • Name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  • Value: your secret key
Use in workflow: ```yaml name: Deploy on: [push] jobs: deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - name: Deploy to AWS env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }} AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }} run: aws s3 sync ./build s3://my-bucket ```

4️⃣ HashiCorp Vault (teams)

For centralized management of secrets in production.

Installation

```bash # macOS brew tap hashicorp/tap brew install hashicorp/tap/vault # Start the dev server vault server -dev ```

Store a secret

```bash vault kv put secret/myapp/config api_key=abc123 db_password=secret ```

Read a secret

```bash vault kv get secret/myapp/config ```

5️⃣ Best practices

  • Regular rotation: Change API keys every 90 days
  • Minimum scopes: Gives strictly necessary permissions
  • Different secrets per env: Dev ≠ Staging ≠ Production
  • Audit logs: Trace who accesses secrets

🎯 Conclusion

Secret management = security 101. Checklist:
  • ✅ .env in .gitignore
  • ✅ .env.example committed
  • ✅ GitHub Secrets for CI/CD
  • ✅ Regular key rotation
> "A committed secret is a compromised secret." 🔐

title: Optimize your builds with Makefile or Taskfile
content:
Introduction: Automate without repeating

Do you type the same long commands every day? Makefile or Taskfile = your centralized CLI interface.

1️⃣ Makefile (classic Unix)

Create Makefile

```makefile # Makefile .PHONY: install dev build test clean deploy install: npm install dev: npm run dev build: npm run build test: npm test clean: rm -rf node_modules dist deploy: npm run build aws s3 sync ./dist s3://my-bucket ```

Usage

```bash make install make dev make deploy # build + deploy S3 ```

Variables

```makefile ENV ?= dev REGION := us-east-1 deploy: @echo "Deploying to $(ENV) in $(REGION)" aws s3 sync ./dist s3://my-bucket-$(ENV) ``` Usage: make deploy ENV=prod

2️⃣ Taskfile (modern, multi-OS)

Installation

```bash # macOS brew install go-task/tap/go-task # Linux sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d ```

Create Taskfile.yml

```yaml # Taskfile.yml version: '3' tasks: install: desc: Install dependencies cmds: - npm install dev: desc: Start dev server cmds: - npm run dev build: desc: Build for production cmds: - npm run build deploy: desc: Deploy to S3 deps: [build] cmds: - aws s3 sync ./dist s3://my-bucket ```

Usage

```bash task install task dev task deploy # Auto-build before deploy ```

3️⃣ Advanced tasks

Docker workflow

```yaml tasks: docker:build: desc: Build Docker image cmds: - docker build -t myapp:latest . docker:run: desc: Run container cmds: - docker run -p 3000:3000 myapp:latest ```

Lint + format

```yaml tasks: lint: desc: Lint code cmds: - eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx format: desc: Format code cmds: - prettier --write "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" check: desc: Run all checks deps: [lint, test] ```

4️⃣ Makefile vs Taskfile

Makefile:
  • ✅ Present everywhere (Linux/macOS)
  • ✅ Known classical syntax
  • ❌ Mandatory tabs (source of errors)
  • ❌ Less readable for beginners
Taskfile:
  • ✅ YAML (more readable)
  • ✅ Multi-OS (Windows, Linux, macOS)
  • ✅ Variables and powerful templating
  • ❌ Installation required

🎯 Conclusion

Make/Taskfile = unified interface for your project. Recommendation:
  • Simple project: npm scripts
  • Multi-language: Taskfile
  • Legacy/Unix: Makefile
> "The best command is the one you don't have to retype." ⚙️

title: Back up and synchronize your dev config between machines
content:
Introduction: Your environment everywhere

Nothing is more frustrating than changing machines and losing all your configs. Objective: New laptop = environment ready in 10 minutes.

1️⃣ Dotfiles with Git

Create dotfiles repo

```bash cd ~ mkdir dotfiles && cd dotfiles git init # Copy important configs cp ~/.zshrc . cp ~/.gitconfig . cp ~/.vimrc . git add . git commit -m "Initial dotfiles" git remote add origin https://github.com/user/dotfiles git push -u origin main ```

Install on new machine

```bash git clone https://github.com/user/dotfiles ~/dotfiles cd ~/dotfiles # Create symbolic links ln -s ~/dotfiles/.zshrc ~/.zshrc ln -s ~/dotfiles/.gitconfig ~/.gitconfig ```

2️⃣ GNU Stow (automation)

Dotfiles structure

```bash ~/dotfiles/ zsh/ .zshrc git/ .gitconfig vim/ .vimrc ```

Usage

```bash # Install Stow brew install stow # Create links automatically cd ~/dotfiles stow zsh # Creates ~/.zshrc stow git # Creates ~/.gitconfig stow vim # Creates ~/.vimrc ```

3️⃣ at home (multi-machine)

Installation

```bash brew install chezmoi # Initialize with an existing repo chezmoi init https://github.com/user/dotfiles # View changes chezmoi diff # Apply chezmoi apply ```

Benefits at my place

  • Templates (different configurations per machine)
  • Encrypted secrets
  • Installation scripts
  • Auto update from GitHub

4️⃣ VS Code Settings Sync

Automatically synchronizes:
  • Extensions
  • Settings
  • Keybindings
  • Snippets

Activation

1. Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P → “Settings Sync: Turn On” 2. Log in with GitHub 3. ✅ Automatic sync!

5️⃣ Full installation script

```bash #!/bin/bash # install.sh # Homebrew /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)" # CLI tools brew install git zsh starship fzf bat exa # Dotfiles git clone https://github.com/user/dotfiles ~/dotfiles cd ~/dotfiles && stow zsh git # Oh My Zsh sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/master/tools/install.sh)" echo "✅ Setup complete!" ```

6️⃣ Files to backup

Essentials:
  • .zshrc / .bashrc
  • .gitconfig
  • .vimrc / .nvimrc
  • .ssh/config
Optional:
  • ~/.config/starship.toml
  • ~/. aws/config
  • Brewfile (Homebrew package list)

🎯 Conclusion

Save your config = tranquility assurance. Recommended workflow:
  • Dotfiles → Git + Stow
  • VS Code → Settings Sync
  • install.sh script for new laptop
> “Each machine becomes your home in 10 minutes.” 🏠

title: Discover little-known CLI tools that make life easier (fzf, bat, exa, tldr, etc.)
content:
Introduction: Modernize your CLI

The CLI is full of little little-known gems that speed up your daily life. Objective: Replace classic Unix commands with modern versions.

1️⃣ fzf – Fuzzy Finder

Interactive fuzzy search in history, files, processes...

Installation

```bash brew install fzf # Keybindings (Ctrl+R for history) $(brew --prefix)/opt/fzf/install ```

Usage

```bash # Recherche fichier vim $(fzf) # Search history Ctrl + R # Interactive cd cd $(find . -type d | fzf) ```

2️⃣ bat – cat with syntax highlighting

cat with syntax highlighting and numbering.

Installation

```bash brew install bat # Alias alias cat='bat' ```

Example

```bash bat src/app.ts # Automatic syntax highlighting bat --theme=GitHub src/app.ts ```

3️⃣ exa – modern ls

ls with colors, icons and Git info.

Installation

```bash brew install exa # Aliases alias ls='exa --icons' alias ll='exa -lah --icons --git' alias tree='exa --tree --icons' ```

Example

```bash exa -lah --git # List + Git statuses exa --tree # Arborescence ```

4️⃣ tldr – Man pages simplified

man but in an ultra-condensed version with examples.

Installation

```bash brew install tldr ```

Example

```bash tldr tar # Quick tar examples tldr git tldr docker ```

5️⃣ ripgrep (rg) – super-fast grep

grep but 10x faster, ignores .gitignore automatically.

Installation

```bash brew install ripgrep ```

Example

```bash rg "useState" src/ # Search in src/ rg -i "api" . # Case insensitive rg -t ts "interface" # TypeScript files only ```

6️⃣ httpie – ergonomic curl

curl but with readable syntax and colored JSON.

Installation

```bash brew install httpie ```

Example

```bash # GET http https://api.github.com/users/octocat # POST JSON http POST https://api.example.com/users name=John email=john@example.com # Headers http GET https://api.example.com Authorization:"Bearer token123" ```

7️⃣ htop – top visual

top with colorful and interactive interface.

Installation

```bash brew install htop ```

Usage

```bash htop # Interactive interface (F9 to kill, F6 to sort) ```

8️⃣ ncdu – disk space analyzer

of but visual and navigable.

Installation

```bash brew install ncdu ```

Usage

```bash ncdu / # Analyze disk space ```

9️⃣ Install all in one command

```bash brew install fzf bat exa tldr ripgrep httpie htop ncdu ```

🔟 Recommended Aliases

In ~/.zshrc: ```bash # Modern replacements alias cat='bat' alias ls='exa --icons' alias ll='exa -lah --icons --git' alias tree='exa --tree --icons' alias grep='rg' alias top='htop' alias du='ncdu' alias curl='http' # Helpers alias preview='fzf --preview "bat --color=always {}"' ```

🎯 Conclusion

These tools do not have a graphical interface, but offer incomparable speed and precision. Must-have:
  • fzf: File navigation
  • bat: Reading code
  • exa: Listing files
  • ripgrep: Search code
> "Modern CLI is faster than any GUI." ⚡

title: Figma for developers: models and design systems
content:
Introduction: Figma is not just for designers

Figma is the collaborative design tool par excellence. As a dev, understanding Figma = better collaboration with designers.

🎨 Key features for devs

Inspect Mode

  • See exact CSS/spacing
  • Export assets (SVG, PNG)
  • Copy hex/rgba colors

Design Tokens

Reusable design variables:
  • Colors: primary, secondary, accent
  • Typography: font sizes, weights
  • Spacing: 4px, 8px, 16px...

Components & Variants

The designer creates components (Button, Card) with variants (primary, secondary). → You implement them the same way in code!

🔗 Figma → Code

Useful plugins

  • Figma to Code: Generates React/Vue/HTML
  • Anima: Export responsive code
  • Zeplin: Handoff design → dev

Figma API

Retrieves design tokens programmatically: ```javascript const response = await fetch('https://api.figma.com', { headers: { 'X-Figma-Token': 'YOUR_TOKEN' } }); ```

💡 Designer-dev collaboration

Best practices:
  • Direct comments on Figma (as code review)
  • Link sharing with specific version
  • Shared design system (Tailwind CSS + Figma)
Figma = common language between design and dev! 🎨

title: Concept: organize your monitoring and projects
content:
Introduction: The all-in-one tool

Notion combines notes, databases, wikis and project management.

📚 Use cases for devs

1. Technology monitoring

Creates an “Articles to read” database:
  • Columns: Title, URL, Category, Status
  • Filter by category (React, DevOps, AI...)
  • Kanban view: To read / In progress / Read

2. Personal documentation

  • Reusable code snippets
  • Solutions to common errors
  • Git/Docker commands memo

3. Side project management

Project template:
  • Idea / Roadmap
  • Technical stack
  • TODOs (database with statuses)
  • Useful resources / links

⚡ Powerful Features

Code blocks

Syntax highlighting for 50+ languages! ```python def hello(): print("Hello from Notion!") ```

Linked databases

A "Projects" database can reference a "Technologies" database.

Templates

Create templates for:
  • Meeting notes
  • Postmortems of incidents
  • Feature documentation

🔗 Integrations

  • API concept: Automate with Zapier/n8n
  • Notion Web Clipper: Saving articles
  • GitHub sync: Issues → Notion

💡 Recommended setup

Main pages:
  • 🏠 Dashboard (overview)
  • 📚 Knowledge Base (personal docs)
  • 🚀 Projects (side projects)
  • 📖 Monitoring (articles/videos)
  • 💼 Freelancer (clients, invoices)
Notion = second brain for developers! 🧠
